supplements.name: Bell's Palsy (Facial Nerve Paralysis)
supplements.notes: Onset December 2024. As of September 2026 (~21 months), face is not notably droopy — just slightly — but there is an extreme downward pressure sensation, like someone pulling downward on the face. Bell's palsy is acute peripheral facial nerve (CN VII) paralysis, usually caused by viral reactivation (HSV-1 or VZV) and/or inflammation compressing the nerve within the bony fallopian canal of the temporal bone.

supplements.name: Elevated CRP (C-Reactive Protein)
supplements.notes: Lab confirmed 9/15/2026 (Quest): CRP 74.8 mg/L (ref <8.0), ESR 56 mm/h (ref ≤30). Extremely elevated — normal CRP is <3 mg/L. WBC is normal (9.7), arguing against active bacterial infection. CALCIUM is 11.3 mg/dL (HIGH, ref 8.6-10.4) — confirms D3-induced hypercalcemia. eGFR 53 (LOW, ref ≥60) — Stage 3a kidney disease, likely from hypercalcemia. The high calcium is likely driving CRP via NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Hemoglobin 12.8 and hematocrit 38.7 are low-normal for a male, consistent with anemia of chronic inflammation.

interactions.title: Multiple Antiplatelet Agents: Bleeding Risk
interactions.description: This stack layers multiple blood-thinning mechanisms: krill oil (omega-3s), black seed oil (2,000 mg — antihypertensive/antiplatelet), trans-resveratrol (200 mg — antiplatelet), quercetin (50 mg — antiplatelet), astaxanthin (mild antiplatelet), and curcumin (200 mg from Protaflo — antiplatelet and anti-coagulant). Curcumin re-enters the stack via Protaflo after the Spike Tri Support was removed. While the fibrinolytic agents (nattokinase, bromelain) are still absent, curcumin at 200 mg with BioPerine (which boosts curcumin absorption by up to 2,000%) is a meaningful antiplatelet addition.
interactions.recommendation: Curcumin is back in the stack via Protaflo, with BioPerine enhancing its absorption. Physician should know about the full antiplatelet stack before any surgery or dental procedures.

interactions.title: CONFIRMED: D3 at ~102,800 IU Causing Hypercalcemia & Kidney Damage
interactions.description: LAB CONFIRMED 9/15/2026: Calcium 11.3 mg/dL (HIGH, ref 8.6-10.4), eGFR 53 (LOW, ref ≥60 — Stage 3a kidney disease), BUN 26 (HIGH), Creatinine 1.16 (HIGH). Total D3 ~102,800 IU/day is causing hypercalcemia DESPITE ~9,280 mcg K2. The K2 is not enough to prevent calcium buildup at this D3 level. The hypercalcemia is now causing a cascade: (1) kidney damage (eGFR 53 = Stage 3a CKD — calcium deposits damaging renal tubules), (2) inflammation via NLRP3 inflammasome activation (contributing to CRP 74.8), (3) neuromuscular dysfunction (likely worsening Bell's palsy 'downward pressure' sensation through muscle hypertonicity). The Coimbra Protocol requires strict low-calcium diet, 2.5L+ daily water, and regular bloodwork — without that dietary support, this dose is causing measurable organ damage.
interactions.recommendation: THE D3 DOSE MUST BE REDUCED. Hypercalcemia and kidney damage are confirmed by lab. Discuss with physician immediately — a supervised reduction to 10,000-20,000 IU/day while monitoring calcium and eGFR is reasonable. The kidneys need to recover (eGFR 53 is reversible if caught early). Continue K2 at current dose during the taper. Recheck calcium, eGFR, and 25(OH)D in 4-6 weeks after dose reduction.

interactions.title: Iodine Intake at 600 mcg: ~4x RDA, Monitor Thyroid
interactions.description: 600 mcg of iodine is about 4x the RDA (150 mcg), still below the upper tolerable limit (1,100 mcg) but getting meaningful. The multivitamin adds ~15 mg (likely listed as 15 mcg based on label) of additional iodine. At this dose, there is a real risk of thyroid disruption in people with underlying thyroid conditions — both hypothyroidism (Hashimoto's) and hyperthyroidism (Graves') can be triggered or worsened by iodine supplementation above 500 mcg. The Wolff-Chaikoff effect (transient hypothyroidism from iodine excess) is a concern at this level.
interactions.recommendation: Still below the UL but warrants thyroid function monitoring (TSH, free T4). Watch for symptoms of thyroid dysfunction: fatigue, weight changes, temperature sensitivity, or heart rate changes. If thyroid issues exist, this dose may be too high.

interactions.title: Zinc-Copper Imbalance (~72.5 mg Zinc)
interactions.description: Zinc from all sources: picolinate 50 mg + multi 7.5 mg + Protaflo 15 mg = ~72.5 mg total. This is nearly 2x the upper tolerable limit (40 mg) and back up from the 57.5 mg after the prior zinc reduction. The Protaflo prostate formula adds 15 mg zinc picolinate. Total copper is still only ~2.75 mg (Thorne 2 mg + multi 0.75 mg). The zinc:copper ratio is now ~26:1 vs. the ideal 10-15:1. Chronic high zinc causes copper deficiency anemia and neurological damage.
interactions.recommendation: Zinc is back up to 72.5 mg due to Protaflo. Consider dropping the standalone zinc picolinate to 25 mg (or eliminating it since Protaflo and multi provide 22.5 mg), or increasing copper to 4 mg to improve the ratio.

interactions.title: Multiple Natural BP-Lowering Agents
interactions.description: Several supplements in this stack lower blood pressure through different mechanisms: magnesium (vasodilator, ~209 mg elemental), potassium (1,020 mg — counteracts sodium), moringa (BP-lowering), and black seed oil (2,000 mg — antihypertensive). With tadalafil removed from the stack, the strongest vasodilator is gone. These natural agents are individually mild but together create a meaningful BP-lowering combination, especially when fasting or dehydrated.
interactions.recommendation: Much safer without tadalafil. Still worth monitoring blood pressure, especially when combining moringa and black seed oil. Watch for dizziness when getting up quickly.

interactions.title: Multiple Mild Blood-Sugar-Lowering Agents
interactions.description: Several supplements have mild blood-sugar-lowering effects: moringa, black seed oil, chromium (40 mcg from multi), and ALCAR. Individually these are minor, but together they create a moderate glucose-lowering stack, especially when fasting or exercising.
interactions.recommendation: Low risk without the dedicated blood sugar formula and berberine. Monitor if diabetic or on glucose-lowering medication.

interactions.title: Immune Stimulation from Multiple Sources
interactions.description: Several immune-stimulating compounds in the stack: elderberry and echinacea are immune activators, black seed oil is an immune modulator, L-lysine and vitamin C support immune function. For someone with autoimmune conditions, this level of immune stimulation could trigger or worsen flares. Echinacea is specifically cautioned in autoimmune disease.
interactions.recommendation: If there is any autoimmune history, consult an immunologist before continuing this combination.

interactions.title: Iron Absorption Blocked by High Zinc and Minerals
interactions.description: The Codeage multi contains iron (27.5 mg). Zinc (~72.5 mg total from 3 sources), calcium, and magnesium all compete with iron for absorption. High zinc is the primary blocker — zinc and iron share the same intestinal transporter (DMT1), and at 72.5 mg zinc, iron absorption is significantly impaired. Protaflo's curcumin (200 mg with BioPerine) also chelates iron, similar to the EGCG that was removed with the Spike Tri Support. Magnesium and calcium add further competition.
interactions.recommendation: Take iron 2+ hours away from zinc, calcium, magnesium, and the Protaflo supplement. Or take iron with vitamin C to enhance absorption.

interactions.title: Synergistic: D3 + K2 + Magnesium
interactions.description: This is a well-designed synergistic combination. K2 directs D3-mobilized calcium to bones and away from arteries. Magnesium is required for D3 metabolism (converts D3 to active 1,25-dihydroxy form). However, the D3 dose itself is the concern — the support stack is good.
interactions.recommendation: Good combination — just address the D3 dose.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Complete B-Vitamin Coverage
interactions.description: The standalone B vitamins (B1, B2, B3, B6, B12) plus those in the multivitamin provide thorough B-complex coverage. B vitamins work synergistically and are water-soluble (excess is excreted). Benfotiamine (B1) and P5P (B6) are superior bioavailable forms. Methylcobalamin (B12) is the active form. This is a well-constructed B-vitamin protocol.
interactions.recommendation: Good selection of forms. Monitor B6 total intake — keep under 100 mg/day long-term to avoid neuropathy.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Glutathione + Vitamin C
interactions.description: Vitamin C recycles oxidized glutathione back to its active reduced form. Liposomal glutathione has better absorption than standard. This is a solid antioxidant foundation.
interactions.recommendation: Good combination for antioxidant support.

interactions.title: Magnesium from 3 Sources: ~209 mg Elemental
interactions.description: Magnesium from 3 sources: L-threonate (~144 mg elemental), glycinate (~50 mg), multi (15 mg). Total supplemental elemental Mg ~209 mg, well within the 350 mg UL from supplements. Well-distributed across bioavailable forms.
interactions.recommendation: Spread magnesium doses throughout the day. Total is within safe range.

interactions.title: Trans Resveratrol 200 mg Adds to Antiplatelet Load
interactions.description: The NMN combo contains 200 mg of trans-resveratrol — a mild antiplatelet agent at this dose. Combined with krill oil (omega-3s), it adds another antiplatelet mechanism. Curcumin (200 mg from Protaflo with BioPerine) has re-entered the stack as an antiplatelet agent, though the fibrinolytic agents (nattokinase, bromelain) are still absent.
interactions.recommendation: The antiplatelet load has increased slightly with Protaflo's curcumin. Mention to physician before surgery.

interactions.title: CoQ10 from 2 Sources: ~25 mg Supplemental
interactions.description: CoQ10 from multivitamin (25 mg) and naturally in beef organs. Total supplemental CoQ10 ~25 mg plus dietary. This is a modest, safe level with mild cardiovascular support.
interactions.recommendation: CoQ10 at this level is beneficial. No concerns.

interactions.title: Rhodiola + Saffron: Serotonin & Dopamine Overlap
interactions.description: Rhodiola rosea increases serotonin and dopamine by inhibiting MAO enzymes. Saffron also affects serotonin reuptake (similar mechanism to SSRIs). Together they create a mild serotonergic combination. If combined with any antidepressant medication, there is a risk of serotonin syndrome — symptoms include agitation, rapid heartbeat, high temperature, and muscle twitching.
interactions.recommendation: Safe together at these doses for most people, but do NOT combine with SSRI/SNRI antidepressants without physician approval.

interactions.title: Synergistic: TMG + B12 + Folate Methylation Support
interactions.description: TMG (trimethylglycine) donates methyl groups to convert homocysteine to methionine. B12 (5,000 mcg) and folate (from the multi) support the same pathway via a different route. Together they provide comprehensive methylation support — important for DNA repair, detox, cardiovascular health, and myelin synthesis for Bell's palsy nerve repair. TMG also helps compensate for methyl group depletion from NAD/NMN supplementation. The increased B12 dose makes this methylation support even more robust.
interactions.recommendation: Excellent synergy, especially alongside the NAD supplement and for nerve repair. The TMG dose is appropriate for the high B12.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Astaxanthin + Glutathione + Vitamin C
interactions.description: Astaxanthin is one of the most potent antioxidants found in nature, working in both water- and fat-soluble environments. Combined with glutathione (the body's master antioxidant) and vitamin C (which recycles glutathione), this trio provides excellent multi-layer antioxidant protection.
interactions.recommendation: Strong antioxidant combination. Astaxanthin at 12 mg is a well-studied, safe dose.

interactions.title: Astaxanthin + Quercetin: Minor Antiplatelet Addition
interactions.description: Astaxanthin has mild antiplatelet effects. Quercetin (50 mg in the NMN combo) also mildly inhibits platelet aggregation. While individually minor, they add to a stack that also includes krill oil, resveratrol (200 mg), and curcumin (200 mg from Protaflo). These minor agents compound the antiplatelet load tracked in int-01.
interactions.recommendation: Low risk individually. These are mild antiplatelet agents that compound the curcumin and resveratrol in int-01.

interactions.title: Zinc-Copper Ratio Worsened (~72.5 mg Zinc): Demyelination Risk
interactions.description: Total zinc is back up to ~72.5 mg/day (picolinate 50 mg + multi 7.5 mg + Protaflo 15 mg) — nearly 2x the UL of 40 mg. Total copper is only ~2.75 mg (Thorne 2 mg + multi 0.75 mg), giving a zinc:copper ratio of ~26:1 vs. the ideal 10-15:1. Copper deficiency causes demyelination — stripping the protective myelin sheath around nerves. For a facial nerve damaged by Bell's palsy (since December 2024), copper depletion actively undermines nerve repair and could contribute to the persistent 'extreme downward pressure' sensation at 21 months.
interactions.recommendation: Zinc has worsened with Protaflo. Consider dropping the standalone zinc picolinate entirely — the multi (7.5 mg) and Protaflo (15 mg) already provide 22.5 mg, which is closer to the RDA of 11 mg. At minimum, increase copper to 4+ mg. Test serum copper and ceruloplasmin levels urgently.

interactions.title: CONFIRMED: Hypercalcemia (11.3) Worsening Bell's Palsy Symptoms
interactions.description: LAB CONFIRMED 9/15/2026: Calcium 11.3 mg/dL (HIGH). The 'extreme downward pressure' sensation at 21 months now has a likely explanation. Calcium is the trigger for muscle contraction — at 11.3 mg/dL, excess calcium causes continuous low-grade contraction and muscle hypertonicity in ALL muscles, but the damaged facial nerve side is most vulnerable. The facial nerve (CN VII) controls the muscles of facial expression — calcium dysregulation at the neuromuscular junction on the affected side directly produces abnormal muscle tone, contracture (synkinesis), and the 'pulling downward' sensation. Additionally, the high calcium is driving systemic inflammation (CRP 74.8) which maintains nerve compression within the bony fallopian canal. The D3 at 102,800 IU/day is causing a triple hit on the facial nerve: (1) hypercalcemia-driven muscle dysfunction, (2) inflammation-driven nerve compression, (3) kidney damage (eGFR 53) reducing the body's ability to clear inflammatory waste products.
interactions.recommendation: REDUCING D3 IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT CHANGE FOR BELL'S PALSY RECOVERY. The hypercalcemia is confirmed and is likely the primary driver of persistent symptoms. As calcium normalizes, expect: less facial pressure, reduced muscle hypertonicity, lower CRP (less nerve inflammation), and improved kidney function. This is the most treatable cause of the persistent symptoms.

interactions.title: Synergistic: B Vitamins + Lion's Mane + ALCAR + Magnesium — Nerve Repair Arsenal
interactions.description: This is the strongest nerve-repair combination in the stack. B12 methylcobalamin (5,000 mcg — increased to therapeutic dose) is critical for myelin synthesis and nerve regeneration — the single most important supplement for Bell's palsy recovery. Lion's Mane (1,000 mg) stimulates nerve growth factor (NGF) — directly promotes nerve regeneration and remyelination, making it one of the most targeted supplements for Bell's palsy. B1 benfotiamine (600 mg) supports nerve energy metabolism and reduces neuroinflammation — the doubled dose strengthens this nerve support significantly. B2 riboflavin (400 mg) supports mitochondrial function in nerve cells. B6 P5P (25 mg) supports neurotransmitter synthesis needed for nerve signaling. ALCAR (1,500 mg) crosses the blood-brain barrier and directly supports nerve regeneration and mitochondrial function in nerve cells. Magnesium L-threonate crosses the blood-brain barrier and is neuroprotective. For Bell's palsy recovery at 21 months, this combination actively supports facial nerve regeneration.
interactions.recommendation: Excellent foundation for nerve recovery. B12 is now at therapeutic 5,000 mcg — good for active nerve healing. B1 benfotiamine doubled to 600 mg — strong support for nerve energy metabolism. Lion's Mane is the most targeted NGF stimulator available. Keep total B6 under 100 mg/day (currently ~35 mg total including multi — safe). These are the most important supplements to keep taking.

interactions.title: Anti-Inflammatory Agents May Reduce Residual Facial Nerve Edema
interactions.description: The facial nerve runs through the narrow fallopian canal in the temporal bone. Any swelling compresses the nerve. The persistent 'extreme downward pressure' at 21 months suggests residual inflammation or nerve edema. The anti-inflammatory agents include: thymoquinone (black seed oil 2,000 mg), omega-3s (krill oil), quercetin (50 mg from NMN combo), trans-resveratrol (200 mg), and curcumin (200 mg from Protaflo with BioPerine for enhanced absorption). Curcumin is one of the strongest natural anti-inflammatory agents — its return via Protaflo significantly strengthens this stack's anti-inflammatory potency for nerve edema reduction.
interactions.recommendation: Protaflo's curcumin + BioPerine restores meaningful anti-inflammatory support. This is a positive addition for facial nerve edema. The fibrinolytic agents (nattokinase, bromelain) are still absent, keeping the bleeding risk tradeoff favorable.

interactions.title: Immune Stimulants vs Bell's Palsy: Viral Clearance or Autoimmune Harm?
interactions.description: Bell's palsy is most commonly triggered by viral reactivation — HSV-1 or varicella-zoster virus (VZV) reactivating in the geniculate ganglion near the facial nerve. L-lysine (3,000 mg) specifically inhibits HSV replication by competing with arginine, providing meaningful antiviral support. Vitamin C and elderberry support general immune defense against viral persistence. However, emerging research suggests Bell's palsy may also involve autoimmune-mediated nerve damage. Echinacea (1,300 mg) is a potent immune stimulant that is specifically cautioned in autoimmune conditions. If autoimmune inflammation is contributing to the persistent symptoms at 21 months, echinacea could be actively worsening recovery.
interactions.recommendation: L-lysine is clearly beneficial if viral etiology is suspected. Echinacea is the risk — consider discontinuing given the prolonged Bell's palsy course. An immunologist can test for autoimmune markers to clarify whether immune stimulation is helping or harming.

interactions.title: Mild Vasodilators May Support Facial Nerve Blood Supply
interactions.description: Bell's palsy involves ischemia (reduced blood flow) of the facial nerve compressed within the bony fallopian canal. Improving blood supply could aid recovery even at 21 months — nerve regeneration is slow (~1 mm/day). Magnesium is a vasodilator (~209 mg elemental from 3 sources), and moringa (1,000 mg) lowers blood pressure. With tadalafil removed from the stack, the remaining vasodilation effect is mild but still present.
interactions.recommendation: Mild vasodilation from magnesium and moringa. Without tadalafil, the hypotension risk is minimal and the nerve blood supply benefit is modest.

interactions.title: Synergistic: NMN + Glutathione + Antioxidants Protect Recovering Nerve Cells
interactions.description: Damaged nerve cells generate excess reactive oxygen species (ROS) during recovery, which can further damage the nerve if unchecked. This antioxidant combination provides multi-layer protection: glutathione (master intracellular antioxidant — 500 mg liposomal), vitamin C (recycles glutathione, extracellular protection — 500 mg), astaxanthin (crosses blood-brain barrier, 6,000x more potent than vitamin C — 12 mg), NMN (boosts NAD+ for nerve cell energy and DNA repair — 1,000 mg), and TMG (supports methylation critical for myelin synthesis — 1,500 mg). For a facial nerve recovering from Bell's palsy, oxidative damage is a key barrier to regeneration.
interactions.recommendation: Strong foundation for nerve recovery. Astaxanthin's ability to cross the blood-brain barrier makes it especially valuable for facial nerve protection. TMG's methylation support is critical for myelin repair.

interactions.title: Selenium from 2 Sources: 275 mcg Total
interactions.description: Selenium from 2 sources: multivitamin 75 mcg + Protaflo 200 mcg = 275 mcg total. The upper tolerable limit is 400 mcg/day, and this intake is at 69% of the UL. Selenium is essential for thyroid function and antioxidant defense but chronic excess causes selenosis (hair loss, brittle nails, GI distress, neurological symptoms). Both sources use L-selenomethionine, the most bioavailable form.
interactions.recommendation: 275 mcg is safe but getting closer to the UL. Avoid additional selenium-rich foods in high quantities (Brazil nuts are extremely high — one nut can contain 70-90 mcg). Monitor for selenosis symptoms if dose increases.

interactions.title: BioPerine/Piperine from 2 Sources: 10 mg Total
interactions.description: Piperine (BioPerine) is now at 10 mg total from 2 sources: NMN combo (5 mg) and Protaflo (5 mg). Piperine inhibits CYP3A4 and other drug-metabolizing enzymes, slowing the clearance of many compounds. This doubles the previous piperine load. The main practical effect: curcumin absorption increases up to 2,000% with piperine (a designed feature of Protaflo), and resveratrol absorption also increases significantly. With tadalafil removed, there is no prescription medication in the stack for piperine to dangerously amplify.
interactions.recommendation: No prescription drug interaction concern now that tadalafil is removed. The enhanced absorption of curcumin and resveratrol is generally positive. If any new prescription medication is added, inform the physician about the 10 mg piperine load — it affects the metabolism of many drugs.

interactions.title: Anti-Inflammatory Stack May Help Lower CRP from 75 mg/L
interactions.description: CRP at ~75 mg/L indicates severe systemic inflammation (normal <3 mg/L). This stack contains several evidence-based CRP-lowering agents: curcumin (200 mg from Protaflo with BioPerine enhancing absorption up to 2,000%) — meta-analyses show curcumin significantly reduces CRP; thymoquinone (black seed oil 2,000 mg) — clinical trials show CRP reduction; omega-3 fatty acids (krill oil 2,000 mg) — strong evidence for lowering CRP, especially EPA; trans-resveratrol (200 mg) — anti-inflammatory via SIRT1 activation and NF-κB inhibition; quercetin (50 mg) — inhibits inflammatory cytokine production. Together these attack inflammation through multiple pathways: NF-κB inhibition, COX-2 reduction, cytokine suppression, and SIRT1 activation. This is the most important therapeutic combination in the stack given the CRP level.
interactions.recommendation: These anti-inflammatory supplements are critically important given CRP at 75. Curcumin + BioPerine is the strongest agent here. However, supplements alone are unlikely to normalize a CRP this high — the underlying cause (infection, autoimmune, etc.) must be identified and treated. Get comprehensive bloodwork including ESR, ANA, RF, CBC with differential, and procalcitonin to differentiate infectious vs. autoimmune causes.

interactions.title: Immune Stimulants with CRP at 75: Potentially Dangerous
interactions.description: With CRP at ~75 mg/L, the immune system is already massively activated — inflammation is the immune system's output. Echinacea (1,300 mg) is a potent immune stimulant that increases cytokine production, including IL-6 — the very cytokine that drives CRP production in the liver. Elderberry (500 mg, 10:1 extract = 5,000 mg equivalent) also activates immune pathways. If the elevated CRP reflects autoimmune inflammation (which overlaps with the Bell's palsy presentation), these immune stimulants are actively worsening the condition. Even if the CRP is from infection, overstimulating an already hyperactivated immune system risks cytokine storm-like escalation. The combination of immune stimulants and a CRP of 75 is like throwing gasoline on a fire.
interactions.recommendation: STRONGLY consider discontinuing echinacea immediately given CRP at 75. Elderberry is less concerning (more antiviral than immunostimulatory) but should also be evaluated. The immune system does not need stimulation — it needs modulation. An immunologist should determine whether the inflammation is autoimmune before continuing any immune-activating supplements.

interactions.title: CONFIRMED: D3 → High Calcium → High CRP → Persistent Bell's Palsy (The Chain)
interactions.description: Labs confirmed the full chain: D3 at 102,800 IU/day → calcium 11.3 (HIGH) → NLRP3 inflammasome activation → CRP 74.8 (9x the threshold for 'significant') → ongoing inflammation compressing the facial nerve at 21 months. The persistent Bell's palsy is NOT just slow healing — it is being actively maintained by supplement-driven inflammation. The normal WBC (9.7) confirms this is not infection-driven inflammation. The ESR at 56 (nearly 2x normal) confirms the inflammation is chronic, not acute. Most Bell's palsy resolves in 3-6 months when inflammation subsides — this one hasn't because the inflammation hasn't subsided, because it's being fueled by D3-induced hypercalcemia. The answer was in the supplement stack all along.
interactions.recommendation: The path to Bell's palsy recovery is now clear: reduce D3 → calcium normalizes → CRP drops → facial nerve inflammation resolves → symptoms improve. This is the most treatable and actionable finding. Discuss D3 dose reduction with physician immediately. MRI with gadolinium contrast can confirm active nerve inflammation if needed.

interactions.title: CONFIRMED: D3-Induced Hypercalcemia (11.3) Driving CRP of 74.8
interactions.description: LAB CONFIRMED 9/15/2026: Calcium 11.3 mg/dL (HIGH). The question of whether D3 was helping or hurting inflammation is now answered — it is HURTING. At 102,800 IU/day, the D3 has pushed calcium above the safe range despite ~9,280 mcg K2. High calcium activates the NLRP3 inflammasome, which drives IL-1β production, which triggers CRP production in the liver. This is likely a major contributor to the CRP of 74.8. The normal WBC (9.7) argues against infection as the primary cause of the elevated CRP, making the hypercalcemia-driven inflammatory pathway even more likely as the main driver. Reducing D3 should lower calcium → reduce NLRP3 activation → lower IL-1β → lower CRP.
interactions.recommendation: D3 dose reduction is now the single most impactful change for lowering CRP. The inflammation is being driven by the supplements themselves, not (primarily) by infection. Reducing D3 to 10,000-20,000 IU/day should normalize calcium within weeks, which should substantially lower CRP. Recheck calcium, CRP, and eGFR in 4-6 weeks to confirm the cascade is reversing.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Antioxidant Defense Against Inflammatory Oxidative Damage
interactions.description: CRP at 75 mg/L means massive oxidative stress — inflammation generates reactive oxygen species (ROS) that damage tissues, proteins, and DNA. This antioxidant combination provides multi-layer protection: glutathione (500 mg liposomal — the body's master intracellular antioxidant, directly neutralizes ROS), vitamin C (500 mg — extracellular antioxidant, recycles glutathione back to active form), and astaxanthin (12 mg — crosses the blood-brain barrier, 6,000x more potent than vitamin C, protects cell membranes). With CRP this high, oxidative damage is ongoing and cumulative. These antioxidants won't lower CRP directly, but they protect tissues from the collateral damage of chronic inflammation.
interactions.recommendation: Important protective role given the extreme inflammation. These antioxidants are especially valuable for protecting the recovering facial nerve from oxidative damage caused by the systemic inflammation. Keep these in the stack.

interactions.title: Zinc-Copper Imbalance May Be Driving CRP Higher
interactions.description: Copper is essential for ceruloplasmin — a major anti-inflammatory and antioxidant protein that also acts as a ferroxidase (prevents iron from generating inflammatory free radicals). With total zinc at ~72.5 mg and copper at only ~2.75 mg (ratio 26:1 vs ideal 10-15:1), copper depletion is likely. Low ceruloplasmin from copper deficiency means: (1) reduced anti-inflammatory capacity, (2) uncontrolled iron-mediated oxidative stress, and (3) impaired antioxidant defense — all of which RAISE CRP. Additionally, copper deficiency causes neutropenia (low white blood cell count), which paradoxically triggers compensatory inflammatory signaling. The zinc-copper imbalance could be a significant contributor to the CRP of 75, not just a bystander.
interactions.recommendation: Test serum copper AND ceruloplasmin levels urgently. If copper is depleted, the zinc-copper imbalance may be actively driving the extreme CRP elevation. Consider immediately reducing standalone zinc (the multi + Protaflo already provide 22.5 mg) and increasing copper supplementation to 4-6 mg to restore the ratio. This is one of the most actionable items in the stack.

interactions.title: Synergistic: Methylation Support Lowers Homocysteine-Driven Inflammation
interactions.description: Elevated homocysteine is an independent driver of inflammation and raises CRP. TMG (1,500 mg) donates methyl groups to convert homocysteine to methionine via BHMT pathway. B12 methylcobalamin (5,000 mcg) and folate (from multi) support the parallel MTHFR pathway. Together they provide comprehensive homocysteine-lowering support. While homocysteine is unlikely to be the primary cause of a CRP this high, it could be a contributing factor — especially relevant given the NMN (1,000 mg) in the stack, which depletes methyl groups and can raise homocysteine if not balanced by TMG. This methylation support helps keep one inflammatory pathway in check.
interactions.recommendation: Check homocysteine levels as part of the inflammatory workup. This methylation trio is well-designed and provides modest CRP benefit. The TMG dose appropriately compensates for methyl depletion from NMN supplementation.

interactions.title: CONFIRMED: Stage 3a Kidney Disease (eGFR 53) from Hypercalcemia
interactions.description: LAB CONFIRMED 9/15/2026: eGFR 53 (LOW, ref ≥60), BUN 26 (HIGH, ref 7-25), Creatinine 1.16 (HIGH, ref 0.50-1.05). This is Stage 3a chronic kidney disease. The most likely cause is hypercalcemia (calcium 11.3) from D3 at 102,800 IU/day — excess calcium deposits in renal tubules (nephrocalcinosis), causing progressive kidney damage. With reduced kidney function, several supplements in the stack need attention: potassium (1,020 mg — serum K is 4.5, normal for now, but damaged kidneys struggle to excrete potassium and levels can rise); magnesium (~209 mg elemental — kidneys excrete excess magnesium, reduced clearance increases risk of hypermagnesemia); all kidney-cleared supplements have slower clearance at eGFR 53. The kidney damage is likely REVERSIBLE if D3 is reduced and calcium normalizes — Stage 3a caught early has a good prognosis.
interactions.recommendation: D3 dose reduction is URGENT — not just for CRP and Bell's palsy but to prevent further kidney damage. Monitor potassium and magnesium levels since kidney clearance is reduced. Stage 3a is reversible if calcium normalizes quickly. Recheck eGFR, BUN, creatinine, and calcium in 4-6 weeks after D3 reduction. If eGFR continues to decline, nephrology referral is needed.
